steps: Travel now = 29% × €460 million = €133.4 million; after +15%: €153.41 million.
Studies = 10% × €460 million = €46 million.
Difference = €107.41 million ≈ €107.4 million. Typical error: adding 15 percentage points to the share instead of raising the amount by 15%.

figure.title: Visitors to national science museums (thousands)

mocks.question: By approximately what percentage did the number of visitors to science museums in Belgium increase between Year 1 and Year 3?
steps: Percentage change uses the earlier value as the base: (603 − 516) ÷ 516 × 100.
= 87 ÷ 516 × 100 ≈ 16.9%, i.e. an increase of about 16.9%.
Typical errors: dividing by the Year 3 value (wrong base), or adding the two year-on-year percentage changes (percentages do not add).

figure.title: Translation requests received by a language unit in one month, by source language

mocks.question: What is the ratio of requests from Spanish to requests from English, in its simplest form?
steps: Spanish : English = 30 : 20. Both numbers divide by 10, giving 3:2.
Typical error: reversing the order of the ratio (2:3).

figure.title: Rail routes: distance and average train speed

mocks.question: If the average speed on the Stonebridge–Hillcrest route rose to 110 km/h, approximately how many minutes would the journey save?
steps: Time = distance ÷ speed. Now: 116 ÷ 80 × 60 = 87.0 minutes. New: 116 ÷ 110 × 60 = 63.3 minutes.
Saving = 87.0 − 63.3 = 23.7, i.e. about 24 minutes.
Typical error: assuming journey time falls by the same percentage as speed rises.

figure.title: Grant applications received and approval rate

mocks.question: How many applications from the Netherlands were rejected?
steps: Typical errors: giving the number approved instead of rejected, or reading another country’s row.

figure.title: Translation requests and average turnaround by language unit

mocks.question: What is the average turnaround time per request in the four units combined?
steps: Total requests = 123. Weighted average = 810 ÷ 123 ≈ 6.59 days.
Typical error: the simple average of the four averages (7.50 days) ignores the different group sizes.

figure.title: Delivery van journey between two depots

mocks.question: What was the van’s average speed for the whole round trip?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. Times: 150 ÷ 60 = 2.500 h and 150 ÷ 120 = 1.250 h.
Typical error: averaging the two speeds (90.0 km/h). The van spends longer at the lower speed, so the true average is lower.

figure.title: A supplier’s price in Canadian dollar and the exchange rate

mocks.question: In euro terms, by approximately what percentage has the supplier’s price risen between Year 1 and Year 2?
steps: Typical errors: quoting the 10% rise in local currency, or the change in the exchange rate alone; both ignore the other effect.

figure.title: Unemployment rate (% of labour force)

mocks.question: By approximately what percentage did the unemployment rate in Poland fall between Year 1 and Year 4?
steps: Relative change = (new − old) ÷ old × 100 = (4.8 − 6.9) ÷ 6.9 × 100 ≈ −30.4%, i.e. a fall of about 30.4%.
Typical errors: 2.1 is the change in percentage points, not a percentage change; another is dividing by the later value.

figure.title: Plastic collected for recycling by four municipal schemes this year, and expected annual growth

mocks.question: If the amount collected in Stonebridge grows at its expected annual rate, compounded, approximately how many tonnes will be collected three years from now?
steps: Compound growth: 1,850 × 1.15³ = 1,850 × 1.5209 ≈ 2,814 tonnes.
Traps among the options: simple growth, 1,850 × (1 + 3 × 0.15) = 2,682 t, ignores compounding; compounding for only two years gives 2,447 t; compounding for four years gives 3,236 t.

figure.title: Price of a conference registration in four markets (fictitious prices and rates)

mocks.question: In euros, approximately how much more does a conference registration cost in the most expensive of the four markets than in the cheapest?
steps: Convert every price to euros by DIVIDING the local price by the number of units per €1:
Most expensive (NOK) − cheapest (CAD) ≈ €587.60 − €428.37 = €159.23, i.e. about €159.
Typical errors: ranking the markets by local price (the currencies are not comparable) or comparing the wrong pair of markets.

figure.title: Containers handled at five ports (thousand units)

mocks.question: Which of the following ports recorded the largest percentage increase in containers handled between Year 1 and Year 2?
steps: Percentage change = (Year 2 − Year 1) ÷ Year 1 × 100:
Largest: Midvale. Trap: Northport has the largest increase in absolute terms (+80 thousand), but from a larger base.

mocks.question: What was the total cost of the “Project management” course for Q2 to Q4 inclusive?
steps: Participants Q2 to Q4 inclusive: 12 + 23 + 4 = 39.
Typical errors: including the wrong quarters, using the whole year, or reading the wrong row of either table.

figure.title: Staff by gender in four units

mocks.question: If the total staff of Unit C increases by 25% and the proportion of women stays the same, how many women will Unit C employ?
steps: Unit C has 12 women and 8 men (20 staff).
Shortcut: if the proportion is unchanged, the number of women also grows by 25%: 12 × 1.25 = 15.
Typical errors: applying the whole increase to women only (17) or calculating the number of men instead.

figure.title: Breakdown of an agency’s annual budget (total €405 million)

mocks.question: Next year the Buildings budget is to rise by 5% while all other items stay unchanged. By how much will the Buildings budget then exceed the Translation budget?
steps: Buildings now = 16% × €405 million = €64.8 million; after +5%: €68.04 million.
Translation = 7% × €405 million = €28.35 million.
Difference = €39.69 million ≈ €39.7 million. Typical error: adding 5 percentage points to the share instead of raising the amount by 5%.

figure.title: Cases closed per month by three teams

mocks.question: How many cases would Team North need to close in June for its average over January to June to be exactly 50 cases per month?
steps: For an average of 50 over 6 months, the total must be 50 × 6 = 300.
January–May total = 49 + 52 + 57 + 43 + 36 = 237.
June must therefore be 300 − 237 = 63.
Typical errors: answering with the target itself (50) or with the current average (about 47).

figure.title: Population and public spending on culture in five regions of one country

mocks.question: Which of the following regions had the highest spending on culture per inhabitant?
steps: Spending per inhabitant = spending ÷ population (€ million ÷ million inhabitants = € per inhabitant):
Northern region ≈ €176; Central region ≈ €132; Southern region ≈ €243; Eastern region ≈ €120.
The highest figure is for the Southern region. Trap: the Northern region has the largest total spending, but not the highest spending per inhabitant.

figure.title: Price changes over two years

mocks.question: Compared with the start of Year 1, by what percentage are translation tariffs lower at the end of Year 2?
steps: Successive changes multiply: (1 + 0.2) × (1 − 0.25) = 0.9000.
So the price is −10.0% compared with the start, i.e. about 10.0% lower.
Typical error: adding the two changes (−5%). Percentages applied one after another do not add.

figure.title: Budget for this year and change compared with last year

mocks.question: What was last year’s budget for the “Coastal flood defences” programme?
steps: This year = last year × 1.25, so last year = this year ÷ 1.25.
Typical error: reducing this year’s figure by 25% applies the percentage to the wrong base.

figure.title: A supplier’s price in Canadian dollar and the exchange rate

mocks.question: In euro terms, by approximately what percentage has the supplier’s price fallen between Year 1 and Year 2?
steps: Typical errors: quoting the 8% rise in local currency, or the change in the exchange rate alone; both ignore the other effect.

figure.title: Translation requests received by a language unit in one month, by source language

mocks.question: What is the ratio of requests from Polish to requests from Spanish, in its simplest form?
steps: Polish : Spanish = 125 : 75. Both numbers divide by 25, giving 5:3.
Typical error: reversing the order of the ratio (3:5).

figure.title: Grant applications received and approval rate

mocks.question: If the number of applications stayed the same, how many additional applications from Spain would need to be approved for its approval rate to reach 45%?
steps: Approvals needed = 1,400 × 45% = 630.
Currently approved = 1,400 × 20% = 280. Additional approvals = 350.
Typical error: giving the total number of approvals needed instead of the additional ones.

figure.title: Regional development fund allocations by sector (€ million)

mocks.question: What percentage of the East region’s total allocation went to Culture?
steps: The East region’s total allocation is €2,300 million, of which Culture received €930 million.
Typical errors: dividing by the Culture column total (the region’s share of that sector) or by the remainder instead of the total.

figure.title: Plastic collected for recycling by four municipal schemes this year, and expected annual growth

mocks.question: If the amount collected in Fairhaven grows at its expected annual rate, compounded, approximately how many tonnes will be collected three years from now?
steps: Compound growth: 6,220 × 1.2³ = 6,220 × 1.7280 ≈ 10,748 tonnes.
Traps among the options: simple growth, 6,220 × (1 + 3 × 0.2) = 9,952 t, ignores compounding; compounding for only two years gives 8,957 t; compounding for four years gives 12,898 t.

figure.title: Unemployment rate (% of labour force)

mocks.question: By how many percentage points did the unemployment rate in Hungary rise between Year 3 and Year 5?
steps: A change in percentage points is the simple difference between the two rates: 12.2 − 10.5 = +1.7 points, i.e. a rise of 1.7 percentage points.
Typical error: computing the relative (percentage) change instead.

figure.title: Visitors to national science museums (thousands)

mocks.question: By approximately what percentage did the number of visitors to science museums in Slovenia increase between Year 1 and Year 3?
steps: Percentage change uses the earlier value as the base: (238 − 209) ÷ 209 × 100.
= 29 ÷ 209 × 100 ≈ 13.9%, i.e. an increase of about 13.9%.
Typical errors: dividing by the Year 3 value (wrong base), or adding the two year-on-year percentage changes (percentages do not add).

figure.title: Delivery van journey between two depots

mocks.question: What was the van’s average speed for the whole round trip?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. Times: 120 ÷ 120 = 1.000 h and 120 ÷ 72 = 1.667 h.
Typical error: averaging the two speeds (96.0 km/h). The van spends longer at the lower speed, so the true average is lower.

figure.title: Index of average house prices (Year 1 = 100)

mocks.question: By approximately what percentage did average house prices in Slovakia rise between Year 3 and Year 5?
steps: With index numbers, the percentage change between two years is (later index − earlier index) ÷ earlier index × 100.
Typical errors: subtracting the indices (16.7 is a change in index points, not per cent) or measuring from the base year (index − 100).

figure.title: Programme spending by sector (€ million)

mocks.question: By how many percentage points did Research’s share of total spending fall between Year 1 and Year 2?
steps: Change = 25.64 − 26.76 = −1.12 points, i.e. a fall of about 1.1 percentage points.
Typical errors: giving the percentage change in the amount spent, or the relative change in the share, instead of the change in percentage points.

figure.title: Candidates and average test score by test centre

mocks.question: What is the average score across all candidates in the four centres combined?
steps: Total candidates = 103. Weighted average = 7,458 ÷ 103 ≈ 72.4 points.
Typical error: the simple average of the four averages (67.8 points) ignores the different group sizes.

figure.title: Rail routes: distance and average train speed

mocks.question: If the average speed on the Lakeside–Westfield route rose to 150 km/h, approximately how many minutes would the journey save?
steps: Time = distance ÷ speed. Now: 160 ÷ 110 × 60 = 87.3 minutes. New: 160 ÷ 150 × 60 = 64.0 minutes.
